candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — N95 respirator versus surgical mask
candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate N95 respirators from surgical masks by recognizing the N95's tight facial seal, fit-testing requirement, and particulate respiratory protection.

options.A: A surgical mask forms a tighter face seal than an N95 and is preferred for inhalation protection from airborne particles.
options.B: A fit-tested N95 is a tight-fitting respirator that filters airborne particles; a surgical mask is loose-fitting and does not provide the same reliable aerosol respiratory protection.
options.C: An N95 and a surgical mask provide equivalent fit and wearer protection from aerosolized particles when both are worn correctly.
options.D: An N95 is intended mainly for splash protection and does not filter small airborne particles.

candidate.rationale: Current CDC/NIOSH healthcare respiratory-protection guidance states that NIOSH Approved filtering facepiece respirators such as N95s are tight-fitting devices that filter at least 95% of airborne particles and require fit testing within a respiratory-protection program. Surgical masks are loose-fitting medical devices that can provide barrier protection against splashes and large droplets but do not provide a reliable level of wearer protection from aerosolized particles because they do not form the same facial seal. Therefore B is correct. A, C, and D misstate the fit or particulate-protection properties of the devices.
candidate.source_claim_supported: A fit-tested N95 provides tight-fitting particulate respiratory protection, whereas a surgical mask is loose-fitting and does not provide the same reliable protection from aerosolized particles.
candidate.source_locator: Healthcare Respiratory Protection > Overview/Respirators: surgical masks are loose-fitting and do not provide reliable aerosol protection; N95 FFRs tightly fit the face, filter at least 95% of airborne particles, and require fit testing. Fit Testing page: filtering facepiece respirators are tight-fitting and fit testing verifies acceptable face-seal protection.
